evidence: Dimension weights: task/tests/scoring.toml [weights] functional=0.6, polish=0.2, visual=0.2 (sum 1.0), gates render/constraints=0.0, [floors] functional=0.05 - byte-identical in content to the frozen template scoring.toml and to the SKILL.md delivery profile, so functional (real behaviour) carries 60% and the two craft dimensions together at most 0.4. Per score.py:46-48 reward = sum(w*score) only when gates pass and functional > 0.05; maximum non-functional contribution is 0.4 < 0.6 functional, so a fully working but plain app (0.6 + partial craft) outranks a polished app with weak function unless functional falls below ~1/3 - the intended shaped policy, template-controlled. Per-criterion functional weights (functional/judge.toml, total 32.0): walls 2.0 x3 (wall_every_route, wall_mentions_and_links, wall_added_live), retention deleted_and_expired_messages 4.0 (two 2.0 parts), timer_changes 2.0, hold_scope_and_release 2.0, persistence 2.0, signin_and_client_scope 2.0; ordinary chat at 1.5 (nested_replies, edits_and_stale_edit, safe_formatting, message_links, unread_and_new_messages_line, live_updates_keep_my_work) and two-part chat criteria at 2.5 (sent_once_in_order, search_and_transcript). Walls+retention = 14/32 (44%), plus client scope and persistence = 18/32 (56%), matching instruction.md 'Two things matter more than anything else. First, ethical walls ... Second, retention'. No functional criterion is weighted below any style criterion's relative share; every criterion is binary on observable behaviour with positive weight. Polish (all 1.0, binary, 5 criteria) and visual (likert: matter_sidebar 2.0, retention_marks 2.0, transcript_page 1.0, phone_chambers 1.0) emphasise the domain-critical surfaces (retention marks, matter list) consistent with the brief. No weight key appears in any [judge] block; gate criteria weight 1.0 under all_pass carry no reward mass. Minor observation (P3, not a ranking defect): the functional weight-rule comment (judge.toml lines ~32-35) says 'a criterion with parts takes their sum' and core legal behaviour is 2.0, yet signin_and_client_scope has Part A (sign-in/sign-out/signed-out replay) and Part B (cross-client replay to M-12) at only 2.0, while deleted_and_expired_messages (two parts) is 4.0 and sent_once_in_order / search_and_transcript (two ordinary parts) are 2.5. Consequence: an app that lets client Gwen read/write M-12 by replay loses 2.0/32*0.6 = 0.0375, slightly less than an app that duplicates a replayed post (2.5/32*0.6 = 0.047). The brief names walls and retention, not client scope, as the top two, and 2.0 still sits at the core level, so this is a self-consistency nit rather than dishonest weighting. Plausible broken app that could pass: a craft-heavy shell with no persistence is excluded by the constraints gate (cross-context post readback) and floor; a pretty app passing one 2.0 criterion scores at most 0.6*2/32+0.4 = 0.4375, below a functionally complete plain app (>=0.6). Conforming alternative that could fail: none created by weights; weights cannot penalise a valid alternative. Runtime reward ordering/discrimination is not measured (raw-evidence-index scope), but that is the subject of rows 40/42, not a requirement of this source-level weight review.
counterexample: Not a Fail. Illustrative self-inconsistency: App X leaks M-12 to a client via replayed requests (fails signin_and_client_scope, weight 2.0) while App Y duplicates replayed posts (fails sent_once_in_order, weight 2.5); X scores 0.0094 higher on the 0-1 reward despite a confidentiality breach.
suggested_fix: Optionally raise signin_and_client_scope to 3.0-4.0 to match the file's own 'parts take their sum' rule (core client-scope Part B at 2.0 plus Part A), or reword the weight-rule comment; no change to scoring.toml.
